title: Describe It First
intro: Morning. One thin stripe of mist holds the ridge.
A teal mug pins the map flat — compass badge to the window.
Papa Bear, our guide, checks the weather, the trail notice, the return time.
I count the torch, the water, the notebook, the spare layer.
verse1: We each carry the route — we turn back if the weather turns.
The mug leans on the map, my finger following the line,
'Harborlight Camp' inked at the top of a page still blank.
We clear the table, take out all that we carried in.
At the entrance I photograph the board, check it against the print;
a shortcut tempts on the left, a brighter hillside on the right —
the wooden marker holds the line, and the ridge stays in sight.
At the overlook you show me the same bridge from a new angle:
short from the shore, long from above — I sketch it both ways,
label where I stood, no need to call either drawing wrong.
Camp on the level ground, the path kept clear, tripod feet checked,
telescope still cased, the mug set back from the table's edge,
notebook clipped so the wind can't turn a page for me.
Then a thin cloud slides across the first evening star —
I had hoped to see everything at once.
'Record the cloud,' you say. 'It's part of the view.'
First entry: pale sky, one bright point, a breeze off the water,
and the page is already useful — it says what we could see.
chorus1: Teal mug down, map flat, page open wide —
describe it first, decide it after;
if the sky won't hold still, write how it moves,
let a glimpse be a glimpse tonight.
verse2: Darkness settles; I lower the lantern,
shield turned to the table — one warm circle of light,
and past its rim the ridge and sky sort themselves out.
You keep the telescope away from the sun's last glow
and we wait for full dark before either of us looks.
We trade turns at the eyepiece.
I describe a bright point — no guess at how far.
'What changed since the last look?' you ask, so I compare:
the cloud has moved, the harbor lights have sharpened,
the pale band over the ridge has faded thin.
Then a streak cuts across while we're both looking up —
no time to catch the whole path, not even between us.
We write the direction, the rough time, one moment long.
Room left for 'not sure' — no grand discovery tonight.
For a while we say nothing; the quiet is part of the watching.
I warm my hands on the mug and add one last line:
waiting gave us a view that hurrying would have missed.
chorus2: Teal mug warm between my hands, lantern down low —
describe it first, decide it after;
a streak, a time, a direction — nothing more,
let a glimpse be a glimpse tonight.
verse3: Before bed the notebook lies open next to the route plan;
every entry names the place, the weather, the time, the watcher —
sketches labeled as sketches, a maybe stays a maybe.
Morning: I count the table — mug, notebook, clip,
lantern, telescope case — and every item's there.
You walk the site for scraps and loose gear — none of it ours.
We leave it clear as we found it, take the same marked path back.
At the overlook the footbridge looks different in morning light,
a third small drawing joins the first page.
The three sketches stand as drawn, nothing erased,
showing how position and light change an honest view.
Home: the teal mug settles beside the folded map,
four pages of notes, three sketches of one bridge,
and one habit — no more dramatic story needed.
bridge: Good notes aren't just for the one who wrote them —
a stranger could pick up this page and read our night:
place, weather, hour, observer — sketches labeled sketches,
a maybe staying a maybe, the streak staying a streak.
Describe it first. Decide it after.
chorus3: Teal mug home beside the map, window open again —
describe it first, decide it after;
four pages, three sketches, nothing erased,
a glimpse stayed a glimpse — and that was the story.
